And in this same year, the ruler of Egypt prepared a certain dark-skinned youth,
who was found to be from the lineage of the Caliph,
and sent him with a small force to come and take Baghdad,
and sit on the throne of his fathers.
He also sent al-Malik al-Salih, the lord of Mosul,
to come to Mosul and sit on his throne.
Because a report had gone out
that the Tatars had perished,
and were wiped out from the earth by the heavenly rod,
and that birds had blinded them—
a tale
that not even old women would believe.
And when the dark-skinned Caliph came near Baghdad,
Ali Bahadur went out with his force, defeated him, and killed him.
And as soon as al-Malik al-Salih entered Mosul on Monday evening (the eve of Tuesday), the seventh of the First Kanun (December),
the Mongols arrived swiftly,
headed by Samdaghu, a Christian Mongol, a splendid youth.
And they surrounded the city on the morning of Tuesday,
when the moon was in Leo.
And they built a wall outside it,
and began to fight fiercely against it.
And the battle against it dragged on until the summer,
and a severe famine occurred in the city.
And the people grew weak from the fighting,
and grew weary in the battles.
And this Samdaghu also began sending them peaceful words,
and was promising good things to al-Malik al-Salih.
And he went out to Samdaghu in parts and in fractions (with great pomp?),
while harpists and mimes were singing and playing before him.
And as soon as he arrived,
Samdaghu had the Mongol forces surround him,
and they entered the city and plundered it,
and slaughtered its inhabitants.
And as for the son of Salih,
that is, Ala al-Mulk,
they gave him wine to drink and made him drunk.
Then they tied a bowstring tightly above his buttocks,
until all his entrails were forced upward.
And they cut him at the band of his loins into two halves,
and they hung the halves above both sides of the portico of the city gate.
They also cut off the head of Muhyi, the son of Ziballaq.
And they took al-Malik al-Salih to the Ordo,
and there he was put to death.
And that aforementioned son of Yunis was made ruler over Mosul.
